newsitem.title: USA: Terra Nova sees net premiums up 40 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Terra Nova sees net premiums up 40 pct in 97.

text.p: Terra Nova (Bermuda) Holdings Ltd said net written premiums rose 26 percent to $311.2 million in 1996 and said a further increase of over 40 percent is expected in 1997.
Terra Nova said 1996 premium growth was helped by the expansion of its participation in Lloyds' syndicates managed by Octavian.

"At a time of growing competition and price pressures in certain lines of business, expansion through a greater involvement in the largely renewal business of these syndicates continues to be the preferred course to optimize earnings going forward," Terra Nova chief executive William Bailey said.
Terra Nova's Octavian Syndicate Management Ltd manages seven Lloyd's syndicates in which the company has a participation.
Net premiums written in the fourth quarter were $35.3 milllion, up 52.1 percent from $23.2 million in the year ago fourth quarter.
An underwriting profit of $7.9 million was reported in 1996 compared with a loss of $9.6 million in 1995, Terra Nova said.

The fourth quarter combined ratio was 96.4 percent compared with 104.5 percent a year ago, largely because of certain expense accruals in the fourth quarter of 1995 which were made throughout 1996, Terra Nova said.

For 1996, the combined ratio improved to 97.2 percent compared with 103.8 percent in 1995, due to a reduction in the loss ratio of 7.1 points offset by an increse in the expense ratio of 0.5 points, Terra Nova said.
